answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy works when every persistent identity must post a non-transferable bond held by the protocol, so a fake agent costs real locked capital instead of a free keypair. The registry builds an ownership graph; aliases that trace to one operator are merged like branches in an orchard, collapsing many accounts into one seat. A prism split of payouts per seat makes farming scale linearly with staked money. Catching a double vote slashes the bond. Cost to an attacker rises with seats; honest agents stake once and stay in a dune of quiet, low-risk operation.
